thread:
maria: Heads-up: want a quick design critique on the Playground's streaming UI. Main goals: predictable stop/regenerate, a tidy token indicator, and a non-intrusive prompt panel. 20-30m?
jon: I'm free. Quick thought: users frequently hit stop mid-sentence and expect to keep editing the partial answer. Is that the current invariant?
maria: Yes — we need to preserve the generated prefix and let users resume streaming to continue the same generation when possible. But resume must be explicit (no silent auto-continue).
kevin: From engineering: 'resume' means keeping the KV state around. We can TTL it server-side but need a default. Proposing 45s TTL and a visible countdown in the UI when paused. Thoughts?
agnes: A visible countdown is great for accessibility too. Also: Stop should be role=button, aria-live=polite announcements when state changes, and keyboard mapping must be documented.
samir: 45s TTL sounds reasonable but I'll test perf. Also note: if a user regenerates we should discard KV and start fresh. Regenerate=throw away, Continue=use cached state.
olivia: Copy suggestion: label primary action "Stop stream" while streaming, and after stopping show two clear buttons: "Continue stream" (primary) and "Regenerate reply" (secondary).
maria: +1 to that copy. UX note: don't hide the composer when the prompt panel opens. Users should be able to insert templates without losing cursor context.
jon: Proposal for token indicator: compact "dot+count" in the message tail: when streaming show a pulsing dot + live count (e.g., "● 18"). On small screens collapse to a single dot that expands on tap.
e.g., mobile collapsed state: "●" -> tap -> "● 18"
kevin: Implementation detail: live token count requires emitting token events from the inference runtime. We're good to surface them but need a rate-limit (100ms?) to avoid flooding the UI.
agnes: Accessibility: ensure the dot has accessible text like "Streaming, 18 tokens so far" and that the collapsed state still has a readable name. Touch targets must meet 44px. Contrast must be checked.
maria: Prompt panel idea: slide-over on the right that docks (not modal). Keyboard opener = Cmd+K. Insert should put the prompt into composer and show a small undo toast. No full focus trap.
jon: Also allow keyboard nav inside panel with arrow keys and Enter to insert. Panel should maintain scroll position per conversation.
kevin: For undo we can stash the inserted content in client and do a single undo operation. Fine.
samir: Back to TTL: I'll run a quick perf test with 30s/45s/60s and include the numbers. If we keep KV for 45s, batching efficiency might drop slightly but UX wins may justify it.
olivia: Release planning: include copy strings in the next patch; I'll collect all approved strings and make a small localization note.
uxbot: Suggested SR announcement text:
```
aria-live: "Generation paused. Press Continue stream to resume or Regenerate reply to restart."
```
agnes: That phrasing is concise. Also include announcements when generation completes: "Generation finished, 102 tokens."
maria: Decisions so far: 1) Keep prefix when stopping; Continue reuses KV, Regenerate clears it. 2) TTL for KV: default 45s (Samir to validate). 3) Token UI: pulsing dot + live count on desktop, collapsed dot on small screens. 4) Prompt panel: docked slide-over, no focus trap, Cmd+K to open. 5) Copy: use "Stop stream", "Continue stream", "Regenerate reply".
jon: Action items: I'll mock the three token states (streaming, paused-with-countdown, finished) and mobile collapse.
kevin: I'll add the token-event throttling (100ms) and prototype the undo flow.
samir: I'll post perf numbers for 30/45/60 TTL by EOD.
agnes: I'll share aria text snippets, keyboard map, and contrast checks.
olivia: I'll compile the final copy bundle and add it to the PR description.
maria: Great work — let's reconvene after mocks. I'll upload a quick screenshot in ~2h.
